html:
The Haiti earthquake of 12 January 2010 had a magnitude of 7.0 and struck near Léogâne, about 25 km west of Port-au-Prince, the capital of Haiti. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in history.

The death toll is disputed. Most estimates range from 100,000 to about 160,000; the Haitian government gave figures as high as 316,000. Some 250,000 homes collapsed, along with the National Palace, the cathedral and the headquarters of the United Nations mission. Over a million people were left homeless and lived in tent camps for months or years.

Haiti was already the poorest country in the Americas, with weak buildings and a weak state. The roots of that poverty go back to the debts and isolation that followed the Haitian Revolution.

Billions of dollars in aid were pledged, but much of it went through foreign groups, and rebuilding was slow. In October 2010 a cholera epidemic began, brought by UN peacekeepers from Nepal. It killed nearly 10,000 people. The United Nations admitted its part only in 2016.
sum: The Haiti earthquake of 12 January 2010 had a magnitude of 7.0 and struck near Léogâne, about 25 km west of Port-au-Prince, the capital of Haiti. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in history.
